scope: Additive Qurʾān, hadith and athar source notes for the scholarly Darūrī only: complete historical dictionary articles and clearly invoked sources in Bidāya applications. No edition files have been modified by this preparation script.
page_number_note: PDF and printed page numbers refer to the frozen 259-page scholarly PDF. After reflow, use the term/article and exact English anchors rather than these old page numbers.
publication_conventions: English publication copy is in each note’s text field; source_urls and source_references supply verified source locator metadata.
Dictionary quotations belong to the named lexicographers. Do not attach their embedded reports to Ibn Rushd’s authorial section merely because the glossary links to that section.
Retain every complete historical dictionary article, its Arabic quotation, translation, source attribution, and existing editorial note. Add source notes outside the historical quotation.
Keep the existing Bidāya book/chapter/issue citations. New application notes identify a report or verse actually invoked in the application; cf. marks a representative parallel where appropriate.
Report numbers follow the linked editions. No source citation by itself implies authentication. Earlier lexical witnesses are explicitly distinguished from independent transmissions.
Use only for the scholarly edition. Do not add this apparatus to the non-scholarly Arabic, vowelled, English, or study editions.
